record.title: Coupled resonators: loading, voltage gain and the complete source budget
record.question: Can passive magnetically coupled resonators produce receiver voltage above source voltage while all receiver power remains accounted for by the source and losses?
record.incoming_evidence: Atlas V4 checked a single RLC circuit but not a coupled receiver or reflected source impedance. Tesla's coupled tuning is a source-grounded mechanism; it does not imply source-free energy.

state_and_units.R: series resistances including receiver load, ohm

model.phasor: Z(omega) I = (V,0); Z11=R1+i(omega L1-1/(omega C1)); Z22=R2+RL+i(omega L2-1/(omega C2)); Z12=Z21=i omega M. Phasors are peak amplitudes; average power uses 1/2.
model.transient: qdot=i; L idot=(Vpeak sin(omega0 t),0)-diag(R1,R2+RL)i-diag(1/C1,1/C2)q; q(0)=i(0)=0.
model.storage: E=(i^T L i + q^T diag(1/C)q)/2, with |k|<1 ensuring positive definite L.
model.budget: Psource=Re(V conjugate(I1))/2; Pload=RL |I2|^2/2; Ploss=(R1|I1|^2+R2|I2|^2)/2. Finite-time source work = load heat + winding heat + stored-energy change.
model.boundary: Ideal sinusoidal source, lumped linear elements, no core hysteresis, stray capacitance, radiation, temperature dependence, source impedance beyond R1, sensor loading or environmental drive.

observables: Receiver power/source real power for nonzero source power
Reflected impedance and complete transient work balance
rival_explanations: Voltage gain is an impedance/phase effect supplied by source power
Apparent excess could arise by comparing peak voltage to real power or omitting source backaction
controls: Zero coupling gives zero receiver response
Zero source gives zero phasor response
Reverse M: receiver phase flips by pi; powers unchanged
At common uncoupled resonance, compare complex currents against closed-form reflected-resistance expression
Double both winding resistances and inspect efficiency reduction at fixed omega0 and nominal RL
Two transient sample spacings and tighter solver tolerance; perform external Simpson work quadrature, not only integrated work states

acceptance.gain_witness: Report at least one fixed parameter row with voltage gain >1 AND efficiency <=1; if absent report failure rather than tune beyond frozen domain.

record.falsifier: Any reproducible passive-model budget violation beyond declared tolerance rejects this implementation; voltage gain alone cannot support a free-energy claim.
limits: Finite fixture and frequency/load grid are not a global optimization theorem
No apparatus has been built or measured
The lumped circuit has no gravity or cosmological degree of freedom

model.forward: I=Z^-1 e with the checked R1 nominal Z; both actual source port voltages are unknown for inference. Source knob values are not substituted for measured source voltages.
model.identifiability: Report domain dimension4 and real ranks/nullities. For nonlinear squared-amplitude maps distinguish local Jacobian kernels at the nonzero fixture from exact finite phase-rival families; zero-current boundary has rank0 for those squared maps.
model.exact_rivals: Full receiver complex current is unchanged by I→I+(delta,0), e→e+Z(delta,0). Both current magnitudes are unchanged by I→(I1,exp(i phi)I2), e→Z I'. Verify changed source vectors reproduce identical restricted observations.
model.coherent_reconstruction: ehat=Zhat Ihat; calibrated full complex map rank4. For secondary reconstruction with only M uncertain and |δIj|≤epsilon_j, bound |ehat2-e2| ≤ omega |Mhat| epsilon1 + |Zhat22| epsilon2 + omega ΔM (|Ihat1|+epsilon1). All other component parameters exact in this bounded model.
model.phase_artifact: Set true e2=0. Rotate only measured I2 by each frozen phase error and reconstruct ehat2. Compare exact artifact Z22 I2(exp(i phi)-1) with numerical inversion.
model.boundary: No cosmological field, stochastic detector noise, calibration drift, instrument transfer uncertainty beyond specified disk/M bounds, nonlinear material response or unmeasured additional port.

controls: Nominal two-current complex reconstruction returns injected source voltages
Explicit exact phase-rival and receiver-kernel examples
Analytical real Jacobians with ranks and kernel witnesses for all four maps; distinguish zero-current squared-amplitude rank0
128 boundary fixtures: 8 phases per independent current error times two M error endpoints; evaluate deterministic disk inclusion, no probabilistic coverage claim
Zero receiver drive with phase error creates a nonzero reconstructed receiver drive
Compare bounded disk exclusion of zero for nominal injected signal; unknown calibration means withhold unconditional signal claim

acceptance.positive_control: Nominal5mV fixture with stated bounds excludes zero; absence must be reported, not repaired by retuning parameters.

terms.label: Inductance
terms.plain: Inductance tells how current stores magnetic energy.
terms.meaning: A scalar coil coefficient or symmetric inductance matrix, according to the attached contract.
cautions: Drawing diameter and turns are not a measured inductance.

terms.label: Mutual inductance
terms.plain: Changing current in one coil can induce voltage in another.
terms.meaning: The signed cross-coil coefficient; its sign depends on the chosen winding/dot convention.
cautions: Mutual coupling does not supply energy.

terms.label: Coupling coefficient
terms.plain: Coupling describes how strongly two modeled coils interact.
terms.meaning: In this passive positive-definite two-coil fixture, M = k√(L1 L2) and |k| < 1.
cautions: A selected k is not a measured coil calibration.

terms.label: Capacitance
terms.plain: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
terms.meaning: The capacitance coefficient; it is not the mathematical field of complex numbers ℂ.
cautions: C as capacitance differs from C used for coulombs or ℂ.

terms.label: Resistance and useful load
terms.plain: Resistance converts electrical energy to heat.
terms.meaning: The receiving load and winding/internal losses are accounted for separately.
cautions: R1 can also name a research round; ℝ denotes real numbers, not resistance.

terms.label: Electric charge
terms.plain: Charge measures how much electricity has accumulated.
terms.meaning: q is an instantaneous scalar or vector; its time derivative is current.
cautions: The unit C means coulomb here, not capacitance.

terms.label: Electrical current
terms.plain: Current is the flow rate of electric charge.
terms.meaning: Lowercase i(t) is instantaneous; uppercase I is a phasor whose peak/RMS convention must be declared.
cautions: The imaginary unit i in an impedance equation is a different meaning.

terms.label: Voltage and source-port drive
terms.plain: Voltage is electrical potential difference between two points.
terms.meaning: Instantaneous voltages and complex source-port phasors are distinct representations.
cautions: A source knob is not automatically a measured port voltage; declare peak or RMS.

terms.label: Angular frequency
terms.plain: Angular frequency counts how quickly a cycle turns through angle.
terms.meaning: One cycle is 2π radians, so ω = 2π f.
cautions: Radians per second and hertz differ by 2π.

terms.label: Impedance and reactance
terms.plain: Impedance describes opposition to an alternating current.
terms.meaning: Complex impedance combines resistance with reactive phase response; X = ωL − 1/(ωC) in the host series circuit.
cautions: Voltage magnification across storage elements is not power gain.

terms.label: Real average power
terms.plain: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred.
terms.meaning: Real average source power uses the real part of voltage times conjugate current, with a convention-dependent factor.
cautions: Peak phasors need a factor ½; RMS phasors do not.

terms.label: Stored energy
terms.plain: Energy can remain in the capacitor and magnetic field.
terms.meaning: Initial and final stored states belong in a finite-time source-work budget.
cautions: Released initial energy is not unexplained energy production.

terms.label: Work transferred over time
terms.plain: Work is energy transferred during a chosen interval.
terms.meaning: Integrating signed instantaneous power gives work; uppercase W here is a variable, while W after a number is the watt unit.
cautions: Lowercase w in the witness contract denotes a voltage, not work.

terms.label: Root mean square
terms.plain: RMS is the square root of the mean squared signal.
terms.meaning: For a pure sine only, peak amplitude is √2 times RMS. For a fixed resistor, RMS determines average heating.
cautions: RMS is not the arithmetic mean or a universal peak conversion.

terms.label: Peak amplitude
terms.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
terms.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

terms.label: Phase and coherent readout
terms.plain: Phase locates one repeating signal relative to another.
terms.meaning: Coherent complex readout preserves relative amplitude and phase under a declared shared reference.
cautions: Sharing a sample clock does not establish equal gain, stable transfer or calibration.

terms.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
terms.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
terms.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Voltage reconstruction-error disk
terms.plain: A deterministic disk bounds how far the estimated voltage can be wrong.
terms.meaning: The supplied current/component error radii are propagated into a complex voltage-error radius.
cautions: This is not a statistical confidence region or a claim of sensor calibration.

terms.label: Imaginary unit
terms.plain: The imaginary unit represents a quarter-turn in complex arithmetic.
terms.meaning: j² = −1; imported contracts often write i instead. It is not electrical current i(t).
cautions: Interpret i from its equation context, not from its character alone.

terms.label: Phasor
terms.plain: A phasor combines a sinusoid’s size and phase into one complex number.
terms.meaning: It represents a single-frequency sinusoid under an explicitly selected peak or RMS convention.
cautions: A phasor is not an instantaneous waveform or automatically a physical electromagnetic field.

terms.label: Complex and real-number domains
terms.plain: A complex number has a real and an imaginary part.
terms.meaning: Two complex source values have four real coordinates: ℂ² is represented by ℝ⁴.
cautions: ℂ is not capacitance C; ℝ is not electrical resistance R.

terms.label: Real part, imaginary part and conjugate
terms.unit: same unit as the complex quantity
terms.plain: These operations separate or reverse parts of a complex number.
terms.meaning: For z = a + jb, Re(z)=a, Im(z)=b and conjugate(z)=a−jb.
cautions: The a and b here are generic coordinates, not automatically witness transfer parameters.

terms.label: Magnitude and squared magnitude
terms.unit: signal unit; its square for squared magnitude
terms.plain: Magnitude measures the size of a complex quantity without its phase.
terms.meaning: For z=a+jb, |z|²=a²+b²; measuring magnitude discards phase information.
cautions: A² is squared amperes here; it is not a new kind of current.

terms.label: Estimate, difference and time derivative
terms.plain: Marks over a symbol tell you which version, change or bound is meant.
terms.meaning: A hat denotes an estimate; δ often a difference or perturbation; Δ can denote a final-minus-initial change or a supplied error bound, according to the contract; a dot is a time derivative.
cautions: Δa and ΔM in these contracts are error-bound radii, not temporal changes. Every symbol needs declared units; ż is velocity, not position.

terms.label: Matrix, transpose, diagonal and inverse
terms.plain: A matrix collects several linked equations into one map.
terms.meaning: Transpose T swaps rows/columns; diag forms a diagonal matrix; inverse undoes an invertible map.
cautions: A matrix inverse is not defined at a singular parameter choice.

terms.label: Rank, nullity and kernel
terms.unit: counts of real or complex dimensions, explicitly declared
terms.plain: Some different inputs can produce exactly the same observations.
terms.meaning: Rank counts independent observed directions; nullity counts unobserved directions; a kernel vector maps to zero.
cautions: State whether dimensions are real or complex. A nonzero kernel defeats unique reconstruction.

terms.label: Jacobian and local reconstruction
terms.unit: output unit / input unit per entry
terms.plain: A Jacobian describes how small input changes affect observations.
terms.meaning: It is the derivative matrix of a nonlinear observation map at one input.
cautions: Local rank does not by itself prove global uniqueness; zero-current boundaries can change rank.

terms.label: Determinant and conditioning
terms.unit: depends on matrix units; dimensionless for witness map
terms.plain: A determinant can reveal when a square map cannot be inverted.
terms.meaning: The witness map is singular when 1−aβ=0; conditioning describes sensitivity near inversion.
cautions: A small numerical residual is not a guarantee of stable physical inference.

terms.label: Positive-definite stored-energy form
terms.plain: A positive-definite energy form is positive for every nonzero state.
terms.meaning: The passive two-coil fixture uses positive L1/L2 and |k|<1 to ensure a positive-definite inductance matrix.
cautions: This declared ideal model does not prove a real apparatus is passive.

terms.label: Numerical sample and grid counts
terms.plain: A grid count says how many numerical evaluations were requested.
terms.meaning: These are computational sampling choices, not counts of physical measurements or participants.
cautions: More grid points do not themselves establish model accuracy or experimental replication.

terms.label: Simulation time window
terms.plain: A time window sets how long the model is evaluated.
terms.meaning: The endpoint and sample counts describe a computational transient, not an operated apparatus.
cautions: A requested sample count and duration do not establish real recorder bandwidth.

terms.label: Normalized frequency domain
terms.plain: A ratio compares the selected frequency with the model’s reference frequency.
terms.meaning: The R1 frequency sweep spans a declared multiple of the nominal resonant angular frequency.
cautions: A ratio is not a new absolute frequency measurement.

terms.label: Positive load sweep domain
terms.plain: The model tries stated receiver-load resistances.
terms.meaning: The positive endpoint domain supports a logarithmically spaced numerical sweep; the reported resistance values still have ohm units.
cautions: A logarithmic grid does not mean the displayed resistance has logarithmic units.

terms.label: Inherited model fixture
terms.plain: A later contract can reuse declared parameters from an earlier model.
terms.meaning: R2 explicitly inherits the R1 nominal circuit; missing values are not independently measured.
cautions: Inheritance is a computational dependency, not independent evidence.

terms.label: SI and unit prefixes
terms.plain: SI is the international system of measurement units.
terms.meaning: cm=0.01 m, mm=0.001 m, µ=10⁻⁶, milli=10⁻³ and nano=10⁻⁹ of the stated unit.
cautions: A source drawing in cm or mm is not silently a metres-based parts table.

terms.label: Scalable Vector Graphics
terms.plain: SVG stores a drawing as shapes and text.
terms.meaning: A vector drawing can retain dimensions and annotations independently of display resolution.
cautions: A precise-looking SVG is not a validated construction drawing.

terms.label: JavaScript Object Notation
terms.plain: JSON stores structured data that can be exported and inspected.
terms.meaning: A receipt encodes declared inputs, outputs and provenance as text records.
cautions: Serialization does not authenticate a claim or measure a device.

terms.label: SHA-256 content digest
terms.plain: A digest helps compare whether two files have the same bytes.
terms.meaning: SHA means Secure Hash Algorithm; the digest identifies content under the named algorithm.
cautions: A matching digest proves neither the truth of content nor its author.

equations.title: Peak and RMS are different conventions
equations.plain: For a sine across a resistor, 1 V peak gives half the heating power of 1 V RMS at the same resistance.
equations.convention: Pure sinusoid; ideal fixed resistor; upstream phasors peak, host circuit input RMS.
equations.units: V, Ω, W; at R=1 Ω: 1 V peak →0.5 W, 1 V RMS →1 W.
cautions: Do not apply the √2 conversion to arbitrary waveforms.

equations.title: Account for all source work
equations.equation: Win = Wload + Wloss + ΔE; E = ½ iᵀLi + ½ qᵀdiag(1/C)q
equations.plain: Source work goes to useful load, heating losses and a change of stored energy.
equations.convention: Instantaneous states and signed finite-time work; no RMS substitution into instantaneous storage.
equations.units: Each work/storage term J; i A, q C, L H, capacitance F.
cautions: Initial stored energy is included. Voltage gain alone is not surplus energy.

equations.title: Average real power from peak phasors
equations.equation: Psource = ½ Re(V conjugate(I1)); Pload = ½ RL |I2|²
equations.plain: The factor one-half converts peak sinusoidal amplitudes into cycle-average power.
equations.convention: Complex peak phasors in upstream coupled-coil contracts; omit ½ only for consistently RMS phasors.
cautions: A complex magnitude discards phase; real source power requires the relative phase.

handbook.title: Coupled-coil energy and phase bench
handbook.overview: An adjustable low-voltage, two-loop bench with complete energy accounting and simultaneous phase-resolved readout.
handbook.goal: Follow the energy supplied to one electrical loop, transferred to a second loop, dissipated as heat and temporarily stored. A higher receiving voltage is not automatically more output energy.
signalSteps: Start with the declared source voltage and the current it supplies to the first loop.
The two coils couple through their magnetic fields. The receiving loop also changes the load seen by the source.
Separate useful-load heating from winding loss and energy still stored in inductors and capacitors.
Compare the complete signed energy account and phase-aware observations, not just the largest displayed voltage.

variables.label: Inductance
variables.plain: Inductance tells how current stores magnetic energy.
variables.meaning: A scalar coil coefficient or symmetric inductance matrix, according to the attached contract.
cautions: Drawing diameter and turns are not a measured inductance.

variables.label: Mutual inductance
variables.plain: Changing current in one coil can induce voltage in another.
variables.meaning: The signed cross-coil coefficient; its sign depends on the chosen winding/dot convention.
cautions: Mutual coupling does not supply energy.

variables.label: Coupling coefficient
variables.plain: Coupling describes how strongly two modeled coils interact.
variables.meaning: In this passive positive-definite two-coil fixture, M = k√(L1 L2) and |k| < 1.
cautions: A selected k is not a measured coil calibration.

variables.label: Capacitance
variables.plain: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.
variables.meaning: The capacitance coefficient; it is not the mathematical field of complex numbers ℂ.
cautions: C as capacitance differs from C used for coulombs or ℂ.

variables.label: Resistance and useful load
variables.plain: Resistance converts electrical energy to heat.
variables.meaning: The receiving load and winding/internal losses are accounted for separately.
cautions: R1 can also name a research round; ℝ denotes real numbers, not resistance.

variables.label: Electric charge
variables.plain: Charge measures how much electricity has accumulated.
variables.meaning: q is an instantaneous scalar or vector; its time derivative is current.
cautions: The unit C means coulomb here, not capacitance.

variables.label: Electrical current
variables.plain: Current is the flow rate of electric charge.
variables.meaning: Lowercase i(t) is instantaneous; uppercase I is a phasor whose peak/RMS convention must be declared.
cautions: The imaginary unit i in an impedance equation is a different meaning.

variables.label: Voltage and source-port drive
variables.plain: Voltage is electrical potential difference between two points.
variables.meaning: Instantaneous voltages and complex source-port phasors are distinct representations.
cautions: A source knob is not automatically a measured port voltage; declare peak or RMS.

variables.label: Angular frequency
variables.plain: Angular frequency counts how quickly a cycle turns through angle.
variables.meaning: One cycle is 2π radians, so ω = 2π f.
cautions: Radians per second and hertz differ by 2π.

variables.label: Impedance and reactance
variables.plain: Impedance describes opposition to an alternating current.
variables.meaning: Complex impedance combines resistance with reactive phase response; X = ωL − 1/(ωC) in the host series circuit.
cautions: Voltage magnification across storage elements is not power gain.

variables.label: Real average power
variables.plain: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred.
variables.meaning: Real average source power uses the real part of voltage times conjugate current, with a convention-dependent factor.
cautions: Peak phasors need a factor ½; RMS phasors do not.

variables.label: Stored energy
variables.plain: Energy can remain in the capacitor and magnetic field.
variables.meaning: Initial and final stored states belong in a finite-time source-work budget.
cautions: Released initial energy is not unexplained energy production.

variables.label: Work transferred over time
variables.plain: Work is energy transferred during a chosen interval.
variables.meaning: Integrating signed instantaneous power gives work; uppercase W here is a variable, while W after a number is the watt unit.
cautions: Lowercase w in the witness contract denotes a voltage, not work.

variables.label: Root mean square
variables.plain: RMS is the square root of the mean squared signal.
variables.meaning: For a pure sine only, peak amplitude is √2 times RMS. For a fixed resistor, RMS determines average heating.
cautions: RMS is not the arithmetic mean or a universal peak conversion.

variables.label: Peak amplitude
variables.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
variables.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

variables.label: Phase and coherent readout
variables.plain: Phase locates one repeating signal relative to another.
variables.meaning: Coherent complex readout preserves relative amplitude and phase under a declared shared reference.
cautions: Sharing a sample clock does not establish equal gain, stable transfer or calibration.

variables.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
variables.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
variables.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

equations.units: V, Ω, W; at R=1 Ω: 1 V peak →0.5 W, 1 V RMS →1 W.
cautions: Do not apply the √2 conversion to arbitrary waveforms.

equations.title: Account for all source work
equations.equation: Win = Wload + Wloss + ΔE; E = ½ iᵀLi + ½ qᵀdiag(1/C)q
equations.plain: Source work goes to useful load, heating losses and a change of stored energy.
equations.convention: Instantaneous states and signed finite-time work; no RMS substitution into instantaneous storage.
equations.units: Each work/storage term J; i A, q C, L H, capacitance F.
cautions: Initial stored energy is included. Voltage gain alone is not surplus energy.

equations.title: Average real power from peak phasors
equations.equation: Psource = ½ Re(V conjugate(I1)); Pload = ½ RL |I2|²
equations.plain: The factor one-half converts peak sinusoidal amplitudes into cycle-average power.
equations.convention: Complex peak phasors in upstream coupled-coil contracts; omit ½ only for consistently RMS phasors.
cautions: A complex magnitude discards phase; real source power requires the relative phase.

whatKnown: This is one proposed setup family with separate R1 forward-energy and R2 reconstruction contracts.
The drawing supplies proposed placement geometry; the contracts separately stipulate numerical component values.

The frozen R1 coupled fixture declares 1 V peak at its source. The separate host series-RLC default declares 0.15 V RMS (root mean square), about 0.212 V peak for a sine. These are different examples and circuit topologies; no normalization or parameter transfer is implied.
whatUnknown: Coil turns, wire gauge, core choice and real parasitic effects are not specified as a validated build.
Actual inductance, mutual coupling, resistance, source impedance and readout loading require measurement.
Component voltage/current/power ratings, tolerances and validated assembly instructions are not supplied by the numerical fixture.
measurementChecklist: Record source voltage, primary current, receiver current and load voltage on a common calibrated timebase.
Record initial and final capacitor voltages and coil currents before comparing finite-time energy.
Characterize signed mutual coupling and both self-inductances at each proposed gap.
Simultaneous source voltage, primary current, receiver current and load voltage with a common timebase and calibrated channel phase.
For transient storage: endpoint currents and capacitor voltages with sign conventions retained.
Separate L1, L2 and signed M characterization at every gap; include winding and source losses.
Receiver loop floats; differential readout must preserve isolation. All sensor burden enters the implemented model.
questions: Does changing the receiving load also change the demand on the source?
Which voltage convention is used: peak phasor or root mean square?
Could omitted stored energy, phase error or sensor loading explain the apparent gain?
